init.title: 1FuseLoader options
init.description: Tune thresholds. Current settings are checked together before saving. Unused phases stay at 0 A. TTL values are seconds; Easee receives rounded-up whole minutes. {error} Current decreases immediately. Fast recovery is on by default: while physically charging, current can rise directly to buffered available capacity after fresh, coherent grid/EV reports. Startup, restart delay and protective reductions still apply. Turn fast recovery off to use the gradual 1 A ramp and its timers. The minimum-current reserve applies at the configured minimum current; the normal buffer applies at higher charging current. Experimental timed overload is off by default. When enabled, the minimum current may continue above the fuse rating within a cumulative budget, after a separate short response window. These settings do not establish the installation's allowable overload or replace physical protection. Short dips, setting changes and restarts do not replenish the budget. The default/manual policy has no automatic budget reset. In manual mode, Start New Overload Trial (7 A) records a new explicit period at 7 A, at most 29 A total and at most 1800 cumulative seconds above 25 A. Two verified checkpoints are required; the vehicle must already be charging with healthy normal-load measurements. The button sends no charger command. Historical exposure and failures remain. Restart, reset, source or policy changes interrupt the period; a manual period never resumes automatically. This is not a fuse temperature model. The start/restart setting is the minimum buffered capacity needed to begin. Once stable, the offer follows verified available capacity up to the configured car maximum, including while waiting for the vehicle. A read-only current/status refresh may be requested when newer evidence is needed for an increase. It is not a short current pulse and does not resume a manual pause or override a vehicle schedule. Conservative import fallback is off by default. Enable only after verifying that grid and car use the same L1 and that the installation has comparable importing loads without generation, storage or cancelling current. Conservative reduction places the entire offer beside raw grid current without subtracting uncertain EV current. Recovery may also raise an accepted offer when raw grid plus the entire new offer fits the ordinary buffer and the other prerequisites are satisfied. This grants no extra overload budget. Observation timestamps and HTTP receipts are tracked separately. Telemetry-stop recovery uses a bounded start offer rather than repeated high-current starts. Bounded nominal reduction is a separate opt-in, off by default. With the experimental profile enabled, an accepted higher cap may be reduced to startup current inside one fixed response window even when an old response latch or spent budget blocks continued overload. New physical response evidence is required; otherwise 0 A is requested and retries are limited. This never replenishes the budget. Under the default response policy, the original response bound of at most ten seconds applies to the minimum-current EV response. With peak-triggered response selected, that electrical countdown is armed only by validated raw L1 above 28 A; ordinary observation does not invent it. A separately selected grid-confirmation wait can follow only after a timely response. The cloud API and minimum one-minute TTL cannot guarantee physical response within the original window. Grid confirmation is a separate opt-in after a qualifying minimum-current EV response within any applicable response deadline. At 0, existing deadlines apply. A positive value permits only a later grid report for at most the selected number of seconds (maximum 30), anchored to the first qualifying minimum-current response. It does not extend the EV response deadline, renew the wait on repeated reports, increase current, replenish exposure or bypass source/current guards. Trial policy changes interrupt an active period; saved history remains. Automatic Overload Cycles is off by default and requires the peak-triggered response policy. With experimental timed overload enabled, healthy raw L1 observations above 25 A for 30 seconds qualify an automatic period. During qualification, extra overload permission requires an EV offer of at most 7 A and sustained L1 of at most 29 A; those first seconds debit the same 1800-second cumulative budget above 25 A. Independently proven normal offers inside the ordinary buffer remain allowed; qualification alone does not force, for example, a safe 12 A reduction down to 7 A. A reading at or below 25 A clears unfinished qualification without refunding time. Re-arm requires fresh, advancing raw L1 below 23 A continuously for 1800 seconds and may also reset a partially used cycle. A reading at or above 23 A, a source gap, rebinding or restart breaks that observation. Lifetime exposure and historical failures remain; current protective faults are not cleared. This is an operational test rule, not verified fuse cooling. The peak response interval and selected post-response grid-confirmation window remain separate; neither is renewed by qualification or re-arming. The manual Start New Overload Trial and End Overload Trial buttons are unavailable in automatic mode; direct calls from an outdated UI are also rejected before any manual trial action.

data.increase_stable_seconds: Gradual mode: stable headroom before increasing (seconds)
data.increase_interval_seconds: Gradual mode: interval between 1 A increases (seconds)
data.overload_margin_amps: Experimental sustained overload above main fuse (A, maximum 4)
data.overload_transition_limit_amps: Experimental peak limit during response window (A, maximum 38)
data.overload_response_seconds: Experimental response window after requesting minimum current (seconds, maximum 10)
data.fast_recovery: Fast headroom recovery (fresh, coherent current reports)
data.nominal_import_only_fallback: Conservative reduction with delayed EV data (verified import-only supply)
data.bounded_nominal_shedding: Bounded lower-current trial after overload lockout (explicit opt-in)
data.peak_only_response: Peak-triggered response policy (10-second emergency only above 28 A; explicit opt-in)
data.grid_confirmation_seconds: Grid confirmation after timely minimum-current response (seconds; 0 = off, maximum 30)
data.automatic_overload_cycles: Automatic Overload Cycles (explicit opt-in; requires peak-triggered response policy)

data_description.meter_envelope_control: Off by default. Requires the verified import-only, peak-triggered automatic overload profile, a car maximum of at most 16 A and a 60 second normal TTL. Uses fresh main-meter load for electrical protection; delayed or inconsistent EV current removes increase credit without by itself stopping an accepted live offer. Genuine source, delivery, lease, peak and cumulative overload protections remain. Enabling this does not reset exposure or start a new overload allowance, resume a manual pause, or establish a fuse cooling guarantee.
data_description.disconnected_readiness: Off by default. While disconnected, keep a normal L1 offer ready only when fresh raw grid current plus the entire offer fits the ordinary buffer. L2 and L3 stay at 0 A. This uses no EV-current subtraction or overload allowance and sends no start or resume command. A fresh connection may adopt the same live, accepted offer without a new restart delay; the vehicle response clock starts only after connection. Source, command-delivery, storage, lease and stronger protective guards still apply. Manual pauses, authorization and schedules are not overridden.
